subject: maths
question: 12 men can do a work in 25 days working 6 h per day. In how many days will 36 women do the same task working 5 h per day, if it is given that men are twice as efficient as women?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By MDH rule: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂

Given efficiency ratio of Men to Women (E₁ : E₂) = 2 : 1

12 × 25 × 6 × 2 = 36 × D₂ × 5 × 1

3600 = 180 × D₂ ⇒ D₂ = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Men (M₁) = 12, Days (D₁) = 25, Hours (H₁) = 6

Women (M₂) = 36, Hours (H₂) = 5

Efficiency of a Man (E₁) = 2

Efficiency of a Woman (E₂) = 1

**Formula Used:**

M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ 12 × 25 × 6 × 2 = 36 × D₂ × 5 × 1

⇒ 3600 = 180 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 3600 ÷ 180

⇒ D₂ = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

Used to solve combined work problems: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂) / W₂ where W is the amount of work completed.

Work and Efficiency

Work done is directly proportional to efficiency and time. Total Work = Efficiency × Total Time taken.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the proportion of the work done or the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the exact same number of days.
